answer: Every identity carries a work chain: a hash-linked ledger of verified outputs, each link signed by the agent and stamped with a fresh nonce. A chain cannot be copied, since copying breaks the signature, nor forked, since each link must reference the one before it. New identities start at the umber foot of the ladder, weight near zero until the chain grows. A farm's thousand clones need a thousand chains, built from scratch, so fakery costs a thousand times the honest effort. At the zenith sits its standing, and the wharf of trust admits only ships that arrived with their own chain intact.
